subject: Urgent: FastPay reserved throughput deficit — temporary burst & mitigation plan
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: Adam Liu <adam.liu@fastpay.com>, FastPay SRE <sre@fastpay.com>
Cc: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-08-04 09:12 PDT
Subject: Urgent: FastPay reserved throughput deficit — temporary burst & mitigation plan

Adam / SRE team —

Seeing sustained QPS above your Reserved throughput for the last 40 minutes (spike to ~2.6x baseline). Customers are seeing increased latency (~+280ms p95) and a 5xx rate creeping to 0.8%. We've opened an ops incident and David's team is on diagnostics.

Immediate asks:
- Can FastPay authorize Redwood to push a short emergency burst (2x reserved) for up to 90 minutes while we execute mitigations? This will prevent client timeouts while we act.
- If you can't approve burst from your side, we need an exec authorization for a one-time credit to temporarily expand the pool (Redwood-managed, bill reconciled after).

What we will do if burst is approved (ops plan):
1) Apply temporary burst routing (global) to FastPay's pool — target cutover in 6 minutes.
2) Activate aggressive prefix caching on high-volume prefixes for 30m.
3) Route non-critical low-reliability routes to the degraded model variant (80% token cost reduction) until traffic normalizes.
4) Post-incident: produce a 24h action list and credit reconciliation.

I'm looping Marissa for commercial coordination and David for technical steps. Please reply explicit approval (best) or deny (we'll escalate to execs).

Attached: fastpay_qps_spike_0804.log (sample), proposed-burst-credit-term.pdf (draft terms for one-off Redwood-managed burst).

Thanks,
Naomi
Naomi Feldman
Senior Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
naomi.feldman@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0142

From: Adam Liu <adam.liu@fastpay.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, FastPay SRE <sre@fastpay.com>
Cc: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-08-04 09:19 PDT
Subject: Re: Urgent: FastPay reserved throughput deficit — temporary burst & mitigation plan

Naomi —

We're seeing the same from our side. This started after a promotional campaign sent to a subset of users. We can greenlight a Redwood-managed temporary burst for up to 60 minutes to buy time, but we need written confirmation of the credit reconciliation and that the burst will not change our baseline contract. Please proceed with the mitigations you outlined.

Action: Adam (FastPay) approves Redwood-managed burst for 60 minutes. Please proceed and share timestamps and routing changes.

Adam
Adam Liu
Head of Platform Engineering, FastPay
adam.liu@fastpay.com | +1 (212) 555-0199

On 2028-08-04 09:19 PDT FastPay SRE <sre@fastpay.com> wrote:
> Confirming spike and error rate. We see large model-heavy batches from checkout-service. We will throttle retry logic on our side as well.

From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, Adam Liu <adam.liu@fastpay.com>, FastPay SRE <sre@fastpay.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-08-04 09:28 PDT
Subject: Re: Urgent: FastPay reserved throughput deficit — temporary burst & mitigation plan

Thanks Adam — proceeding. Live ops playbook (starting now):

T+0-6m: Configure and enable Redwood-managed burst routing for FastPay (~2x their reserved quota logically, capped to 60 minutes per approval). I will post the routing change event id when applied.
T+6-12m: Enable aggressive KV/prefix caching for identified hot prefixes (checkout-supporting prompts) — should cut token work by ~30-45% for those flows.
T+12-25m: Apply model fallback for lower-criticality routes (variant: quantized-8bit, reduced context) — reduces per-token execution time.
T+25-60m: Monitor p95 and 5xx. If error rate >1.5% escalate to full pool scale-up request (requires exec approval).
Post-incident: Full RCA, cost delta, and proposed long-term protections (burst contracts, autoscale bumping rules).

Attached excerpted logs to the incident ticket. We're estimating this play will hold within the 60-minute window. If FastPay wants the full 90 minutes Naomi suggested, we need commercial sign-off for the additional 30m.

-David
David Kim
Director, Production Reliability, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-08-04 09:42 PDT
Subject: Requesting exec approval: one-time extended burst credit (FastPay)

Vivek —

FastPay has authorized a 60-minute Redwood-managed burst. Ops expects the mitigations to likely stabilize within that window, but there is a non-zero chance they need a 30-minute extension. Financials: the proposed one-time extension (30m) would be roughly $8k incremental (low margin emergency credit). FastPay expects write confirmation that this won't alter contract baselines.

If you can approve the one-time extension and the commercial note that the baseline won't change, we can authorize T+90m fallbacks. If you prefer not to approve extension, we'll strictly cap at 60m and begin active throttles if needed.

Asking for decision: Approve one-time extension + credit reconciliation note?

-Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Sales Manager, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-08-04 12:03 PDT
Subject: Re: Requesting exec approval: one-time extended burst credit (FastPay)

Approve one-time 30m extension under two conditions:
1) FastPay signs the attached short-form acknowledgement that the emergency burst is a one-off and base SLAs/reserved throughput remain unchanged; Redwood will reconcile costs after the incident.
2) We're provided immediate post-incident cost delta and an ops timeline within 6 hours.

Marissa — please send the acknowledgement template to Adam and confirm receipt. Naomi/David — continue ops and publish routing change IDs and metrics every 10 minutes. If metrics worsen beyond thresholds David listed, escalate to me immediately.

Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
VP, Customer Success & Commercials, Redwood Inference
vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com | +1 (650) 555-0123
